title: Redwood x CloudBridge marketplace integration sync
summary: Sync to align on Marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture artifacts, joint solution packaging, and next steps for launch. Discussed VPC onboarding, KMS/SOC2 checklist, billing integration, and acceptance tests. Agreed owners for docs, diagram, and test harness; follow-up demo and pricing thread scheduled.
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're at 3pm PT, 25th Oct, quick roll call?
00:05 Asha Raman: Hi this is Asha, PM at CloudBridge.
00:07 Liam O'Connor: Liam here, partner eng.
00:09 Samira Patel: Samira from Redwood, SE.
00:11 Priya Menon: Priya, CloudOps.
00:12 Miguel Torres: Miguel, solutions.
00:14 Evan Brooks: Evan, marketplace product.
00:16 Jordan Lee: Awesome. Goal for today - align on what Redwood needs for the marketplace listing + reference arch and how we package the joint solution. we'll cover technical certs, deploy templates, and acceptance tests.
00:28 Asha Raman: Sounds good. We have a Q4 marketplace launch target so want to make sure there are no blockers.
00:34 Samira Patel: Quick note: there are two paths - hosted integration (we list Redwood-hosted offering) vs bring-your-own (customer deploys Redwood private on their infra and we list integration). Which track do you want to prioritize?
00:48 Evan Brooks: For CloudBridge we want both but start with hosted listing to get the PR and referencing working, then follow with a reference-arch for private/VPC. Typical customers will want the VPC option.
01:02 Jordan Lee: Great. On hosted listing we need listing assets: logo, short/long descriptions, 3 screenshots, support contact, and a validated test purchase flow. We'll share our marketplace checklist after.
01:18 Liam O'Connor: On the technical side we need an auth flow for provisioning — is there an OAuth client or API key flow from Redwood for marketplace provisioning?
01:26 Samira Patel: We support both. For hosted marketplace provisioning we usually issue a marketplace token that maps to a Redwood account and links billing. The token exchange is via a REST callback; we can share the sample webhook.
01:38 Priya (interrupting): quick Q on data residency - if a customer is in eu, hosted offering needs to run in eu-region. Is that supported?
01:44 Miguel Torres: Yes we have EU regions; we can pin region per listing. small caveat: certain model variants may be only in specific regions, we'll include fallback variants.
01:57 Asha Raman: Ok good. Next: reference architecture for private deployment, we need a diagram that shows VPC peering, cross-account roles, and KMS usage. Do you have a terraform module?
02:09 Samira Patel: We have a reference terraform module and CloudFormation snippets; they are in our partner repo. we'll attach the repo link but note it's a bit of a moving target due to runtime optimizations.
02:22 Evan Brooks: Can you include an example that demonstrates dedicated capacity? customers will ask about reserved GPU pools and autoscaling.
02:30 Miguel Torres: yes example will show dedicated GPU pools, autoscaler policies, and a typical 2AZ setup with fallback to hosted for burst. We'll include KV cache notes (sometimes transcribed as key cache) and recommended quantization profiles.
02:46 Liam O'Connor: On security/compliance, CloudBridge requires SOC2/ISO attestation and ability to integrate into our KMS for key wrapping. what's Redwood's stance?
02:56 Hannah Wu: Redwood is SOC2 Type II certified; we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments, and for hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS in some cases. we'll share the security deck.
03:12 Priya Menon: We need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM - any log shipping options?
03:18 Samira Patel: yes audit logs can be exported to S3/CloudWatch/Stackdriver and forwarded; we can provide an example lambda for forwarding to common SIEMs.
03:28 Asha Raman: Great. Acceptance tests - marketplace will run a validation that spins up a trial and hits the inference endpoint with a small prompt set. what benchmarks do you recommend?
03:38 Miguel Torres: For listing we ask for a smoke test: 200 token generation, 10 concurrent users, and 95th percentile latency under the SKU SLO (we'll give numbers). for performance page we can include a link to our benchmark spreadsheet but note that those numbers vary by model and quantization.
03:56 Evan Brooks: Is there a sample harness we can run that's deterministic?
04:00 Samira Patel: we have a reference harness (pytest-based) that hits endpoints and validates outputs, latency, and token accounting. We'll provide it.
04:10 Liam O'Connor: On billing integration - marketplace will collect billing but we need metering hooks so Redwood can credit usage to CloudBridge accounts. Is there a reporting API?
04:20 Jordan Lee: Yes we expose a usage reporting API and can accept postback events. we also support invoice reconciliation via CSV export. We'll map the billing ids to your marketplace account id.
04:32 Asha Raman: timeline wise - we need listing assets + security docs by Nov 1 to make the Nov 15 marketplace review cycle. Is that doable?
04:40 Jordan Lee: doable. We'll aim to send the assets by Oct 29 to give you time.
04:46 Priya Menon: One more ops question - during onboarding can we get a pre-prod sandbox?
04:50 Samira Patel: yes we can provision a sandbox with throttled capacity for validation. It will have a separate API key and sandbox region.
05:00 Evan Brooks: For the joint solution PR, marketing will want a 1 pager and a solution diagram. Miguel, can you own the solution diagram?
05:09 Miguel Torres: yes I'll draft the solution diagram and include typical deployment flows.
05:14 Asha Raman: We'll need a joint runbook for escalations, contact points, and an SLO list.
05:20 Hannah Wu: we'll include an escalation matrix and standard SLOs.
05:24 Liam O'Connor: technical nit: for private deployments we need cross-account IAM roles for the provisioning lambda. any example trust policy?
05:32 Samira Patel: yes we'll include an example trust policy and least-privilege role. sometimes the transcription generator flips role names (we saw 'Redwood role' as 'readwood', lol) but actual policy will be clean.
05:46 Asha Raman: ok sounds like we have owners. can we recap next steps?
05:50 Jordan Lee: recap: 1) Redwood to share marketplace checklist, security deck, terraform module link, and sample provisioning webhook by Oct 29 (owner: Jordan / Samira). 2) Miguel to draft reference architecture diagram and 1-pager by Nov 2. 3) CloudBridge (Asha/Liam) to provide acceptance criteria and marketplace asset templates by Oct 30. 4) Schedule follow-up demo + walkthrough of sandbox on Nov 8. 5) Start joint PR draft (marketing) - Hannah to coordinate.
06:30 Priya Menon: quick clar - does sandbox support customer managed keys?
06:36 Samira Patel: sandbox will have simulated KMS; for full KMS we need a private deployment which we'll document.
06:44 Evan Brooks: any competitor questions? CloudBridge asked about MegaCloud AI's marketplace terms earlier; just to confirm, do we have exclusivity asks?
06:52 Jordan Lee: no exclusivity. We also support co-selling requirements but nothing blocking.
07:00 Asha Raman: thanks everyone. we'll expect the docs and then pick date for Nov 8 demo.
07:05 Jordan Lee: thanks, we'll close out.
07:08 [Meeting ends]
next_steps: Redwood to send marketplace checklist, security deck, terraform module, sample webhook by 2026-10-29 (Jordan/Samira)
Miguel to draft reference architecture diagram + 1-pager by 2026-11-02
CloudBridge (Asha/Liam) to provide acceptance criteria and marketplace asset templates by 2026-10-30
Hannah to coordinate joint PR draft and marketing assets
